title: Mini quant hunches and runnotes
content:
Purpose / quick context:
- Brain dump of small experiments, suspicious regressions, and prompts to try on q4->q8 conversions. Not a polished note — quick log for me before passing to Marco/Lina.
- Priority: find a small quantization setup (4/6/8-bit) that keeps answer formatting for short-chat tasks and doesn't blow up on long context with KV cache.

Recent runs (summary):
- 2026-03-09 11:20 — baseline fp16 (cpu/gpu): base_v1, seq_len=1024, batch=1
  - latency: 42ms/token on A100-40GB (steady), 1.0x baseline cost.
  - qualitative: coherent, passes prompt/QA checks.

- 2026-03-10 09:42 — per-tensor 8-bit (pt-8) with simulated KV cache reuse
  - settings: activation quantization symmetric, weight static min/max per-tensor, no outlier clipping.
  - latency: 33ms/token.
  - failure modes: occasional token repeats at generation boundary (esp. when asked to continue long code blocks).
  - perf metric: EM-style metric on eval set dropped from 87.6 -> 85.1 (small but consistent).

- 2026-03-11 15:05 — per-channel 6-bit (pc-6) with scale sharpening + residual-scaling hack
  - settings: per-channel weight quant, 6-bit linear, median-based clamp for outliers, residual-scale multiplier 1.03
  - latency: 28ms/token (batched), CPU decode still sloopy.
  - perf: some prompts improved (short chat), others catastrophic (long form hallucination increased).
  - weird: attention distributions look "sharper" in head 4 and 11. Need to visualize head-wise KV norms.

Quick hunches / hypotheses to test: (ordered by easiest to try)
1) Re-run pt-8 but with dynamic activation range estimation (EMA) over 50 steps instead of static min/max; suspect activation clipping causing token repeats.
2) Try per-channel 8-bit but with outlier-aware scaling: detect 0.5% largest weight magnitudes and store them in low-rank residual (cheap trick) — should help code continuation.
3) Check KV cache serialization: when restoring KV states across prompt splits, small FP->INT rounding may cause repeated tokens. Add a deterministic "align" step: round KV to 8-bit when loading and then unquantize with same scale.
4) For pc-6 runs, reduce residual-scale multiplier to 1.0 and add layernorm-scale correction before final softmax. Possibly the 1.03 multiplier amplified certain attention logits.

Immediate experiments to run (short commands / notes):
- exp/isha/pt8-ema-50: baseline_pt8 + activation_ema_steps=50, clip_mode=0.999
  - eval subset: chat-short (100 samples), code-continue (50 samples)
  - metrics to collect: ROUGE-L, token-repeat-rates (n=3), avg-perplexity, top1-token-change-rate vs fp16

- exp/isha/pc8-outlier: per-channel-8 + outlier-residual-k=256 (float32 stored small matrix)
  - measure memory overhead and step decode latencies separately.

- exp/isha/kv-align: inject deterministic align into KV load path and re-run pt8 sequences that previously repeated

Notes on prompts and eval sets (copy/paste ready):
- chat-short (example prompts):
  1) "Summarize the following paragraph in one sentence: {para}."
  2) "Give a step-by-step plan for turning {idea} into an MVP under 4 weeks."
  3) "You are an assistant who responds in bullet points only. Rewrite: {input}."

- code-continue (example prompts):
  1) "# Continue the python function to parse nested JSON objects:\n  def parse(obj):\n    # ..."
  2) "/* Complete the JavaScript snippet for a binary search */\n  function binarySearch(arr, target) {\n    // ...\n  }"

Dirty-run log (quick):
- 2026-03-11 18:23 — ran pt8-ema-50 on 20 chat-short samples
  - result: repeat rate down from 6.2% -> 3.1% for short chat.
  - code-continue still fails: truncated output mid-token ~ 12% more than fp16.

- 2026-03-12 08:12 — pc8-outlier on 10 code samples (quick)
  - observed: token-level perplexity improved vs pc6 but still worse than pt8 baseline for code completions.
  - note: decoding speed 1.1x faster than pt8 (noise in measurement).

Debugging ideas / small checks: (one-liners to run)
- plot_kv_norms --model exp/isha/pc6-run1 --layers 0,4,7,11 --heads 4,11
- compare_logits --a fp16-run1 --b pt8-ema50 --sample-id 23 --topk 50
- frame-shift-check: tee generated tokens into hex and diff between fp16 and quantized runs to locate first mismatch

Things I keep forgetting to check (TODO log):
- seed parity between runs (sometimes job runner sets seed differently) — set SEED=12345 in all experiments.
- verify tokenizer version (tokenizer v1.3 vs v1.4 cause off-by-one in byte-pair split for some code strings).
- log CUDA kernel selection: some pc quant kernels fallback to slower path if shapes misalign.

Risks / customer-facing notes (for later write-up):
- Even small formatting regressions in chat (missing punctuation, repeated bullets) are visible in production UI and cause bigger customer complaints than raw accuracy numbers imply. Need to include human-readability checks in experiments.
- For Dedicated/private customers where cost matters, 1.2x speedup at 8-bit is attractive but only if hallucination/token-repeat risk is low.

Next moves (week plan):
- Today: run pt8-ema50 full eval (all subsets), push notes to exp board. (responsible: me)
- Tomorrow: build quick viz for kv-norms and dump head-wise distributions. (collab: Marco)
- By Friday: prototype pc8-outlier with low-rank residual and measure memory/latency. (collab: Lina)

Misc scratch / random observations:
- If we store per-channel multipliers as 16-bit floats instead of 32, decode speed wins but we might lose dynamic range needed for rare heads. Try fp16-scales in a cheap trial.
- Thought: maybe not all layers need pc quant — try hybrid: last 4 transformer blocks kept fp16, earlier ones quantized. Could preserve generation stability while saving memory.

If I forget: ping @Marco or @Lina in slack with subject "isha quant hunch follow-up".

Raw output examples (from quick runs) — include to show what "bad" looks like:
- input: "Finish the sentence: The model predicted that the next step would be"
  - fp16: "The model predicted that the next step would be to run a series of tests and gather feedback."
  - pt8-bad: "The model predicted that the next step would be to run a series of tests and run a series of tests and run a series of tests."

End of note.
